column3: “Cush” is rendered “Ethiopia”; NASB supplies “over.”
“The citadel” is rendered “the capital,” and “the throne of his royalty” as “his royal throne.”
“Made a feast” is rendered “gave a banquet,” “officials” as “princes,” and “servants” as “attendants.” NASB supplies “officers.”
“The wealth of the splendor of his kingdom” is rendered “the riches of his royal glory.”
“From great and unto insignificant” is rendered “from the greatest to the least”; NASB supplies “lasting.”
The Hebrew opens with a list of materials; NASB supplies “There were hangings.” “Rods” is rendered “rings,” and the names of the stones are uncertain.
“They gave to drink” is rendered “Drinks were served,” and “according to the hand of the king” as “according to the king's bounty.”
“Every chief of his house” is rendered “each official of his household,” and “man and man” as “each person.”
“The house of royalty” is rendered “the palace.”
“Was good” is rendered “was merry,” and “said” as “commanded.” “With the face of” is rendered “in the presence of.”
“Good of appearance” is rendered “beautiful.”
“Which was by the hand of the eunuchs” is rendered “delivered by the eunuchs.”
“The manner of the king” is rendered “the custom of the king”; NASB supplies “so to speak.”
“Who saw the face of the king” is rendered “who had access to the king's presence.”
Close to the Hebrew.
NASB moves “in the presence of the king and the princes” forward; “did wrong” is rendered “has wronged.”
“The matter of the queen” is rendered “the queen's conduct,” and “to make despicable … in their eyes” as “causing them to look with contempt on.”
“The noble ladies” is rendered “the ladies”; NASB supplies “will speak in the same way.” “As enough of contempt” is rendered “plenty of contempt.”
“A word of royalty” is rendered “a royal edict,” and “her queenhood” as “her royal position.” “Her fellow woman, the good” is rendered “another who is more worthy.”
“From great and unto insignificant” is rendered “great and small.”
“The word was good in the eyes of” is rendered “this word pleased.” “The word of Memucan” is rendered “as Memucan proposed.”
“Documents” is rendered “letters,” and “writing” as “script.” The last clause is difficult; NASB renders “and the one who speaks in the language of his own people.”
